title: openapi_validator plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `openapi_validator` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component OpenapiValidatorConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

OpenapiValidatorConcreteMediaType.description: Concrete RFC 9110 type/subtype and valid HTTP field value. Wildcard type/subtype, braces in tokens, leading whitespace, malformed parameters, and control bytes other than horizontal tab are rejected. Parameter names require token or quoted-string values.

OpenapiValidatorConfig.description:
Plugin: openapi_validator — validates request parameters (path, query,
header, cookie) and request and response bodies against operation
schemas generated from an attached OpenAPI/Swagger document. Supports
JSON, XML, form-urlencoded, multipart, text, and binary media types.
JSON Schema `format` is asserted under every `schema_draft` (unknown
formats such as OpenAPI's int32/int64/byte/password stay annotations).
Must be proxy-scoped; every config load rejects global and
proxy_group scope. Multipart Content-Disposition accepts ordinary
`filename` or a single bounded RFC 5987/8187 `filename*` (UTF-8 only;
unquoted ext-value) and rejects continuations, quoted `filename*`,
bare/non-token parameter segments, conflicts, and hostile extended
values.
XML conversion honors OpenAPI XML Object fields
`name`, `namespace`, `prefix`, `attribute`, and `wrapped` (namespace
matching uses the URI; `prefix` is serialization metadata only;
members that collide with a modeled name but not its XML construct or
namespace are rejected fail-closed rather than dropped or rebound).
Scalar elements contain text without structural members; namespace
declarations remain valid. A present empty wrapped array becomes [];
array containers reject unmodeled attributes, text, and wrapper children.
UTF-8 binary bodies receive full string-schema validation. Non-UTF-8
binary bodies support boolean schemas, optional string-compatible type,
byte-count minLength/maxLength, format: binary, and the annotations
listed in docs/openapi_validator.md. Other assertions require a text
representation and fail validation for non-UTF-8 bodies.
Usually generated by `x-ferrum-validate` on
`POST /api-specs` or `PUT /api-specs/{id}`; direct creation requires a
proxy-scoped plugin attached to a proxy with `api_spec_id` set.
Strict parameter import is selected with the import-only
`x-ferrum-validate.reject_unsupported_parameters` boolean (default false),
not a field of this runtime config. When true, optional unsupported
parameters refuse spec admission with `400 MalformedExtension` naming
the first affected operation, parameter, and reason; otherwise they are
warned about and dropped. Unsupported required parameters always refuse
import.
Every fixed-field object in this schema is closed: an unknown key at the
root or in `bypass`, `error_response`, an `operations[]` entry, or
`request_body` is rejected at construction so a misspelled enforcement
control cannot silently fall back to a weaker default. An explicit
`null` for a non-null field is likewise rejected instead of selecting
its omission default. Free-form maps
(media types, response status keys, `bypass.header_present`, encoding
property names) stay open but their keys are shape-validated.
Response schema failures emit only a fixed generic message plus the
allowlisted JSON Schema keyword; raw schema locations, backend instance values and
JSON property names never appear in client problem bodies or
`openapi_validator.response_error` metadata.
The REQUEST contract is decided in the dedicated
`validate_client_request_body_contract` lifecycle phase over the original
client representation, before any `before_proxy` hook or request-body
transformer can add, remove, rename, coerce, or replace fields
(`GHSA-896v-jx23-9g6p`). Buffering for that phase is selected from the
matched operation alone, never from a `Content-Type` a client can omit
or mismatch; in `block` mode a missing required body and a nonempty body
with no applicable declared media type both fail closed
(`GHSA-6p78-6x8c-9g9x`).

enforcement_mode.description: Blocking rejects mismatches, log_only records metadata and continues, disabled skips validation.

validate_request.description: Validate request bodies when an operation has a request schema, and request parameters when an operation declares `parameters`.

validate_response.description: Validate response bodies when an operation has a response schema.

request_content_types.description: Request media types in scope. JSON includes `+json`, XML includes `+xml`, text/plain covers `text/*`, and application/octet-stream covers common binary application, image, audio, and video types. An explicitly empty list is rejected; omit the field for the default scope.

response_content_types.description: Response media types in scope. JSON includes `+json`, XML includes `+xml`, text/plain covers `text/*`, and application/octet-stream covers common binary application, image, audio, and video types. An explicitly empty list is rejected; omit the field for the default scope.

fail_on_unknown_operation.description: Reject requests that do not match any generated operation. In block mode the client-visible problem title is "Unknown OpenAPI operation" with detail "No OpenAPI operation matched this request"; the method and path are not interpolated into either string.

fail_on_missing_response_schema.description: Reject a response whose selected response object yields no schema. Applied after status selection to a missing `Content-Type`, a content type outside `response_content_types`, an unmatched declared media type, a body returned for a status with no declared content, and a status covered by no response object. An empty body for an explicitly empty response declaration remains valid. Statuses with no body semantics (HEAD, 1xx, 204, 205, 304) are always skipped. Strict mode still schedules the response hook when every declared response has an empty content map.

max_body_bytes.description: Maximum raw or decompressed body size to validate, 1 to 67108864 (64 MiB). It is also the per-layer decoded ceiling while undoing Content-Encoding, so a larger value is rejected at admission.

schema_draft.description: Sole authoritative JSON Schema draft selector used when compiling every operation's request and response schemas. Per-operation draft fields are not part of the published contract; the importer emits this field only at the top-level config.

operations.description: Generated operation schema table. Required in file mode and other direct plugin configuration; POST /api-specs and PUT /api-specs/{id} generate it from the attached document when x-ferrum-validate is enabled. The importer replaces this from the spec on every spec PUT. Two operations with the same method and the same path_regex are rejected. Within a method, overlapping operations are ordered by literal-segment count, then by the leftmost differing segment (literal before `{template}`), then by document order; `operation_label` never affects selection.

consumers.description: Mapped Consumer usernames that skip validation. An unmapped external identity never matches, even one that spells a listed username.

header_present.description: Header name to shared secret. A request skips validation only when that header carries exactly the configured secret (compared in constant time). Presence alone never skips validation, because clients can send any header, so null is rejected. The secret must be 16 to 4096 visible ASCII characters (0x21-0x7E: no spaces, controls or non-ASCII), so characters and bytes coincide. Bypass header names are redacted from diagnostics and policy calls. Inject it from a trusted hop or gateway plugin and keep it out of client hands. Keys are matched case-insensitively at runtime; case-equivalent duplicate keys are rejected at construction.

unsupported_media_type_status_code.description: Status for a nonempty request body that no media entry declared for the matched operation covers (including a body sent with no `Content-Type` at all). Kept distinct from `request_status_code` so remapping schema failures does not also remap media-type refusals. `log_only` records the same decision and continues.

error_truncate_chars.description: Size bound on the validation diagnostic written to openapi_validator.request_error / openapi_validator.response_error metadata and to the problem body. Only ever narrows: the effective cap is min(error_truncate_chars, 256). This is not a confidentiality control. Admission also enforces the target's usize range. Diagnostics are payload-free by construction and never contain the rejected instance value, an expected enum/const constant, a raw schema path or schema-library / XML-parser rendering, a configured XML name or namespace, a hostile Content-Encoding coding token, a backend Content-Type, the request target, or a payload-chosen JSON/XML/form/multipart member name.

OpenapiValidatorEncodingHeader.description: Multipart Encoding Object header entry. A bare JSON Schema preserves Ferrum's historical required-header form. A Header Object is selected by exactly one of `schema` or `content` and is closed so misspelled presence controls cannot weaken validation. Schema form accepts the OAS schema-form fields (`style`/`explode`/`example`/`examples`). Simple serialization decodes comma-separated arrays and object key/value pairs; explode=true objects use comma-separated name=value members. Content form accepts only the common fields plus `content`. Header-location `allowEmptyValue` and `allowReserved` are rejected. The `content` form requires exactly one concrete media type whose Media Type Object carries `schema`.

content.description: OpenAPI Header Object content map. Exactly one concrete media type is required (no `type/*` or `*/*`). The full key, including any parameters, must be a valid RFC 9110 media type and HTTP header value. The header value is decoded as that media type under multipart header-size limits before schema validation. multipart/form-data is not supported as header content.

OpenapiValidatorEncodingHeaderContentMed.description: Media Type Object inside an Encoding Header Object `content` map. Encoding Objects are not valid on part headers; only schema (plus mutually-exclusive optional example metadata) is accepted.

OpenapiValidatorEncodingMap.description: OpenAPI Encoding Object map keyed by schema property name. Supported for application/x-www-form-urlencoded and multipart/form-data. Unsupported style/explode combinations are rejected at admission. The constructor also checks that every key names a declared schema property, deepObject selects an object, and spaceDelimited/pipeDelimited select an array or object. Exploded object child keys must not overlap root siblings or another exploded object; a free-form exploded object cannot coexist with another exploded object. These schema-dependent checks cannot be expressed by this map component alone.

style.description: Serialization style. `form` (default), `spaceDelimited`, `pipeDelimited`, and `deepObject` are supported. Path/header styles such as `matrix`, `label`, and `simple` are rejected.

explode.description: Defaults to true for `form`, false otherwise. `spaceDelimited` and `pipeDelimited` require explode=false; `deepObject` requires explode=true.

allowReserved.description: OpenAPI allowReserved flag. When false, literal RFC 3986 reserved bytes in form values are rejected and must be percent-encoded (serialization delimiters such as the form explode=false comma remain valid).

contentType.description: Expected multipart part Content-Type (comma-separated list allowed). Only valid for multipart/form-data. Trimmed before use; must be nonempty and at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes after trimming (the byte limit is checked by the constructor).

headers.description: Additional multipart part Header Objects. Present values are validated against their schemas (or against the single media type declared in a Header Object `content` map after decoding under header-size limits); an absent header fails only when its Header Object sets required=true (the OpenAPI default is false). Only valid for multipart/form-data. Must not redefine Content-Type, Content-Disposition, or Content-Transfer-Encoding. Case-equivalent duplicate header names are rejected at construction and during API-spec extraction.

OpenapiValidatorFormEncodingMap.description: Form-urlencoded encodings cannot declare multipart headers or contentType.

OpenapiValidatorJsonSchema.description: JSON Schema value embedded in an openapi_validator operation. Accepts ordinary object schemas and OpenAPI 3.1 boolean schemas (`true` / `false`). Dialect selection is controlled by the top-level OpenapiValidatorConfig.schema_draft field, not per operation.

OpenapiValidatorMediaType.description: Media selector or map key. The base type uses MIME tokens (including braces), permits type/* and */*, trims surrounding Unicode whitespace, and is ASCII case-insensitive. Control characters are rejected anywhere; parameters after the first semicolon are ignored for selection. Lists and maps must be unique after trimming, ASCII lowercasing, and removing parameters. This normalized uniqueness is checked by the constructor; JSON Schema uniqueItems detects only literal duplicates.

OpenapiValidatorMediaTypeContent.description: Request-body content entry. A bare JSON Schema is canonical when no Encoding Object is present. An entry with `encoding` must use the strict Media Type Object shape, preventing ambiguous schema/wrapper parsing.

method.description: Nonempty method, normalized to uppercase by the constructor.

path_template.description: Effective OpenAPI path template used for metadata and path specificity ordering. When generated from a spec, this is the Paths key joined to the effective Server Object pathname (OpenAPI 3.x) or Swagger `basePath`, with the literal proxy listen_path prefix prepended (trailing prefix slashes trimmed). Root, host-only, exact, and regex listen routes add no prefix. One entry is emitted per distinct server pathname when multiple servers apply. strip_listen_path affects backend forwarding only.

path_regex.description: Regex used to match the full inbound request path, compiled at plugin load. Auto-generated specs derive it from the effective path template (including literal listen prefix and server/`basePath` prefix); operator-supplied full-path patterns are not prefixed or stripped and are automatically anchored as `^(?:...)$` (full-path match) so a loose pattern cannot substring-match an unintended superstring path.

operation_label.description: Optional metadata label. Defaults to "`METHOD path_template`".

request_required.description: Reject empty request bodies when the OpenAPI requestBody is required.

content.description: Media type to schema map. Each entry is either a bare JSON Schema (object or boolean) or, when encoding metadata is present, a Media Type Object with required `schema` and `encoding` fields. Keys must be a media type or media range (`type/subtype`, `type/*`, `*/*`). Exactly one of `content` or the `content_type` + `schema` form is allowed; the object is never treated as its own media map.

schema.description: Alternate single-schema form (object or boolean schema).

encoding.description: Alternate single-schema form encoding map. Only valid with application/x-www-form-urlencoded or multipart/form-data.

request_body.description: Request body schemas by media type.

parameters.description: Declared OpenAPI parameters, validated in `before_proxy` when `validate_request` is true. Generated from the operation's and its Path Item's `parameters` (operation entries override Path Item entries with the same `name` and `in`). `in` + `name` must be unique (header names case-insensitively).

responses.description: Status code to media type to JSON Schema map (object or boolean schemas). Response selection is status-first: an exact status code wins, then the narrowest matching OpenAPI wildcard range such as `4XX`, then `default`. A selected response object is final — a media-type miss inside it never falls through to a range or `default` object, because those cover status codes that are not otherwise declared. Media keys must be a media type or media range (`type/subtype`, `type/*`, `*/*`) and are matched most-specific-first. A declared status with an empty media map means the status is declared to carry no content; the importer emits those entries so the precedence rule holds. A status entry may alternatively use the OpenAPI Response Object shape `{description?, content: {mediaType: schema}}`; that form is closed and rejects any other key.

OpenapiValidatorParameter.description: One OpenAPI Parameter Object in the validator's supported subset: each location's default serialization (`simple` for path and header, `form` for query and cookie) over scalar, array-of-scalar, and object-of-scalar schemas. Anything else — another `style`, an array of arrays/objects, or a `form` + `explode: true` object — is rejected at construction (the importer omits such a parameter when it is optional and refuses the import when it is required). Path values come from the canonical request path, query values from the client's raw query string (at most 1024 pairs), header values from the pristine wire request headers (never a header map an earlier `before_proxy` hook mutated), and cookie values from the wire `Cookie` header, percent-decoded per the `form` serialization (at most 1024 pairs); a value that repeats for a non-array schema, a missing required parameter, a value that cannot be converted, or a schema failure is a request violation with `error_response.request_status_code` and the problem title "Request parameter validation failed". Diagnostics name the declared parameter and never contain its value.

name.description: Parameter name, at most 256 bytes without control characters. Path parameters must match a `{name}` expression of `path_template`; header names must be valid HTTP field names other than Accept, Content-Type, or Authorization (which OpenAPI ignores).

required.description: Defaults to true for path parameters (which must be required) and false otherwise.

style.description: Only the location's default style is accepted (`simple` for path/header, `form` for query/cookie).

explode.description: Defaults to true for query/cookie (`form`) and false for path/header (`simple`).

OpenapiValidatorResponse.description: One response status entry, either the generated media-map form or the closed OpenAPI Response Object form.

OpenapiValidatorResponseSchema.description: Response media schemas cannot carry an Encoding Object.
